item.title: Germany: Berlin student protest targets rearmament and compulsory service
item.description: Thousands of students marched through Berlin, on Friday 20 November 2026, protesting against the country's rapid military rearmament and fears of a return to compulsory military service. Their protest formed part of a wider wave of youth demonstrations across Europe.

item.title: Video shows dramatic helicopter rescue of woman trapped in flood channel
item.description: Los Angeles County firefighters rescued a woman trapped in a fast-moving flood control channel using a helicopter and an airborne paramedic.

item.title: Germany intensifies engagement with South Caucasus as 'region of opportunities'
item.description: Germany's foreign minister visited Azerbaijan and Armenia to develop projects of “strategic importance to Europe both economically and politically," in the context of Russia's aggression against Ukraine and the economic situation in Europe.

item.title: Trump defends Putin ties and accuses Iran of dishonesty in negotiations
item.description: Speaking at a White House following his trip to Asia, Trump defended his ties with Xi and Putin, claiming the Russian leader wanted to end the war in Ukraine through diplomacy. He also called for a "real deal" with Iran.

item.title: Thousands protest across Europe demanding better wages and services
item.description: Demonstrations began Friday in over 25 European countries and are expected to continue through the weekend as part of a coordinated international protest movement.

item.title: What do we know about Rwanda return hubs and how effective will they be?
item.description: Five EU countries have announced a controversial plan to set up a centre in Rwanda for migrants with no legal right to stay in Europe. While supporters say it will help governments to deter illegal immigration, critics are concerned about potential human rights violations and a lack of oversight.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU and UK strike post-Brexit reset deal as Russian missiles hit Poland
item.description: The EU and UK have struck a major post-Brexit reset deal in Brussels. In tonight’s edition of Europe Tonight, we bring you a live interview from the summit, assess security alarms after Russian missiles hit Poland, and examine the final-day standoff at COP31.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 20th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 20th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Researchers find that cats tailor their communication to get human attention
item.description: A plaintive meow, a gentle purr or an innocent wide-eyed look: cats clearly know how to get their humans' attention. Scientific studies show that they use surprisingly sophisticated communication strategies.

item.title: Morocco commits €366 million to build a national defence industry by 2035
item.description: The royal cabinet said the plan aims to meet 40% of the armed forces’ and security services’ equipment needs through domestic production by 2035 and to generate more than 65% of industry revenues from exports, supported by a new strategic agency, a holding company, and two new industrial zones.

item.title: Spain requires data centres to draw 80% of their electricity from renewables
item.description: Spain tightens regulation of data centres with new requirements on renewable energy, efficiency and digital sovereignty to limit their impact on the power grid and attract sustainable investment.

item.title: France investigates suspected confidential leaks to Le Pen's far-right party
item.description: A former senior Interior Ministry official is suspected of sharing details of investigations into National Rally's election campaign finances, according a French newspaper.

item.title: Deepening EU–Canada ties: From critical minerals and defence to erasmus+
item.description: ‘We are determined to drive the renewed political momentum between the EU and Canada forward,’ write four Members of the European People’s Party (EPP) Group in the European Parliament in an op-ed for Euronews, published on the occasion of a visit by an EPP delegation to Canada on 19–21 November.

item.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
item.description: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

item.title: Italy: Workers and students stage nationwide strike over living costs
item.description: Workers and students marched through Rome, on Friday 20 November 2026, joining a nationwide strike over stagnant wages, rising living costs and government spending priorities. Protesters also demanded more funding for education and criticised military spending.

item.title: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh pledges ‘relentless diplomacy’ in bid to lead the UN
item.description: Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati star diplomat running to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development, and prosperity. She has pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.

item.title: From Tashkent to Amman: Books and Universities Bring Uzbekistan and Jordan Closer Together
item.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan deepen ties through book launches, academic conferences and university partnerships, highlighting reforms and shared cultural heritage.

item.title: EU Commission partially clears Hungary’s €10bn recovery fund payment after rule of law reforms
item.description: The European Commission says Budapest has met all but one of the conditions for the full €10bn payment. The financial penalty for the missing milestone is expected to be “minimal”, sources told Euronews.

item.title: Ukraine: Rescue teams search wreckage after deadly Russian strike on Kyiv
item.description: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killed eight people on Friday 20 November 2026, according to Associated Press, leaving buildings and warehouses damaged across the capital. Firefighters battled blazes as emergency crews searched the wreckage and police collected evidence.

item.title: Candidate or kingmaker: could ECB President Lagarde influence France's presidential race?
item.description: Lagarde remains bound to political neutrality until her tenure as ECB president ends in February 2027, just two months ahead of the first election round of France's presidential elections.

item.title: Burnham drew a line under Brexit at the EU-UK summit. But where does Britain go next?
item.description: The EU-UK summit delivered landmark agreements at their Brussels summit, but also exposed the limits of negotiating one deal at a time. As Brussels signals its willingness to explore closer ties, Andy Burnham faces a bigger question: how far does Britain want to go?

item.title: Russia stalls UN bid to regulate AI 'killer robots' as talks near deadline
item.description: Campaigners warn the world is approaching an "Oppenheimer moment" over weapons that can choose and attack targets with no human involved.

item.title: NYC mayor unveils plan to close notorious Rikers Island jail by 2032
item.description: Rikers had been slated to close by August 2027 following legislation passed by the City Council in 2019. Moving the deadline will require a change to this law.

item.title: Estonia to shut border with Russia over GRU-linked sabotage attack
item.description: The five checkpoints will close from 1 December, with a possible review in six months, after an attempted arson at a defence facility near Tallinn that Estonian authorities say Russian military intelligence ordered. Rail services will remain unaffected.

item.title: Polish cities sound air raid sirens after Russian missile strike
item.description: Poland says three Russian objects, believed to be two missiles and a jet-powered drone, entered its airspace during an overnight attack on Ukraine. Air raid sirens sounded in the country's east.

item.title: Revisiting Brexit is the 'democratic' and 'honest' thing to do, says MEP Tobias Cremer
item.description: German Socialist & Democrats MEP Tobias Cremer says a majority of Britons believe Brexit "was a mistake" and caused "economic damage" to the United Kingdom.

item.title: Robotaxis in Guangzhou, medical drones in Shenzhen: inside China’s race to scale autonomous transport
item.description: China’s robotaxis now operate commercially in Guangzhou and Shenzhen while drones deliver coffee, medicine and defibrillators, as companies race to take autonomous vehicles from test zones to scale.

item.title: Will e-methanol become a game changer for decarbonising maritime shipping and plastic industries?
item.description: Euronews gained access to the world’s first industrial plant that produces e-methanol on a large scale. The Kassø site in Denmark paves the way for a climate-friendly energy transition — even within hard to abate sectors.

item.title: Norway signs carbon credit deals with Indonesia and Morocco to help fund renewable energy
item.description: Norway’s carbon credit purchases will help finance projects that might otherwise go unbuilt, while allowing it to count emissions cuts towards its own targets.

item.title: Chevron to begin offshore oil and gas exploration in Greece
item.description: Chevron and HELLENiQ ENERGY are set to begin seismic surveys for oil and gas in Greece’s southern Ionian Sea. The results could help determine whether to drill in a country that relies on imported gas.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'You Can See Everything' - Is this Elizabeth Holmes doc 2026's best film?
item.description: Finally arriving to Europe with a staggered theatrical release, this documentary is every bit as strange and fascinating as you've heard.

item.title: Slovenia’s Ljubljana and Majorca’s Calvià named the 2027 European Capitals of Tourism
item.description: The Slovenian capital city was recognised for its resident-focused approach and year-round tourism, while the Majorcan municipality was praised for moving away from mass tourism towards a more sustainable model.

item.title: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché over alleged assassination plot
item.description: Two men linked to one of Denmark's most notorious criminal gangs have been charged over a plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper, prompting a nationwide crackdown on the outlawed group.

item.title: TikTok rolls out deepfake detection tool for public figures to fight back against disinformation
item.description: The social media company’s ‘Likeness detection’ feature is aimed at politicians dealing with the deluge of disinformation online.

item.title: ‘Dream Trips of Europe’: Stunning holiday destinations to visit in 2027
item.description: Lonely Planet’s latest guide highlights journeys spanning ancient history, dramatic natural landscapes, scenic rail routes and some of Europe’s most distinctive food and wine destinations.

item.title: Himalaya-sized ancient 'supermountains' found beneath Antarctica's ice sheet
item.description: The discovery offers a window into the continent's geological past and of how life on Earth has evolved.

item.title: UK anthem returns to the EU stage in symbolic post-Brexit moment
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was welcomed by EU leaders in Brussels for a summit aimed at strengthening post-Brexit relations. God Save the King rang out for the first time since Brexit at the UK–EU summit.

item.title: Furious Farage accuses Burnham of betraying Brexit as EU-UK summit gets underway
item.description: Speaking exclusively to Euronews, the Reform UK leader admitted Brexit had failed to deliver on immigration, but accused Prime Minister Andy Burnham of betraying voters by bringing Britain closer to the EU.

item.title: This vaccine can prevent cervical cancer. Which Europeans actually get it?
item.description: HPV vaccination rates vary by country and gender, EU health data shows.

item.title: In the billionaires club: Ashton Kutcher gets mega rich after Anthropic's Wall Street debut
item.description: Some actors, artists and sports stars are big fans of AI. Actor Ashton Kutcher, Black Eyed Peas singer will.i.am and former NBA player Tristan Thompson are among those reported to have made a fortune from backing Anthropic, the US company behind the Claude AI chatbot.

item.title: Unrest around French cost-of-living protests could cost insurers €207mn
item.description: Damage from the unrest around France's October cost-of-living protests could cost insurers €207 million. France Assureurs says the estimate is "particularly high for events concentrated into 24 hours". Over 95% of the estimated cost relates to damage to business property.

item.title: European Commission staff criticise lack of communication over cyberattack
item.description: The main civil servants’ union has criticized senior management for letting staff learn of the breach from the press, as employees fear their personal data is at risk.

item.title: Bending Spoons to buy Mailchimp from Intuit in €3.35bn deal
item.description: The Italian tech company behind WeTransfer and Vimeo has agreed to buy email marketing platform Mailchimp. Intuit is selling it for less than a third of what it paid in 2021.

item.title: Lufthansa plans 1,000 job cuts in Frankfurt and Munich as Iran war slows turnaround
item.description: Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 full-time jobs in Frankfurt and Munich as strikes and soaring fuel costs linked to the Iran war slow its turnaround. Its flagship airline lost €20 million a month on average from January to September, according to a letter to staff.

item.title: Vatican: Giant Christmas tree lifted into place beside St Peter's Basilica
item.description: A towering 25-metre Christmas tree was lifted into place in St Peter's Square, Vatican City, on Friday 20 November 2026, as preparations began for this year's Christmas celebrations. The silver fir, donated by a community in southern Italy, will be unveiled on 7 December.

item.title: Moving my religion: Vatican Museums explore a century of Popemobiles
item.description: From Pius XI's Mercedes to John Paul II's Popemobile: eight historic cars show how Popes' vehicles have changed. The Vatican Museums exhibition retraces a century of history, between technology, curiosities and safety.

item.title: World is being ‘held hostage by oil mafia’: How one tiny country is putting its foot down at COP31
item.description: On the final day of COP31, one country says it will “not lend its name” to “complacent or ineffective language” in the final pact, which requires consensus.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 20th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 20th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Portugal national public sector strike over pay disrupts key services
item.description: Public administration workers are holding a national strike this Friday, demanding better pay and working conditions. Health, education and justice are among the hardest hit sectors, with many public services likely to face disruption.

item.title: Former French PM de Villepin launches presidential bid, as centrists and conservatives slide in polls
item.description: Dominique de Villepin's presidential bid comes as France's centrists and conservatives have been struggling to gain ground.
